Let the three visible faces of the cube be the **front**, **top**, and **right** faces. They meet at the front-top-right vertex.

### 1. Examine the given cube
- The front-face diagonal contains the common vertex.
- Neither the top-face diagonal nor the right-face diagonal contains that vertex.

Thus, among the three marked faces, **exactly one diagonal must have the common vertex as an endpoint**.

### 2. Fold each net
Tracing the diagonals onto the cube gives:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{Choice} & \text{Arrangement of marked faces} &
\text{Number of diagonals containing their common vertex}\\ \hline
A & \text{three adjacent faces} & 0\\
B & \text{three adjacent faces} & 2\\
C & \text{three adjacent faces} & 3\\
D & \text{three adjacent faces} & 1\\
E & \text{two marked faces are opposite} & \text{not applicable}
\end{array}
\]

Therefore, only \(D\) satisfies the necessary vertex condition.

### 3. Check the orientation of \(D\)
When net \(D\) is folded, its marked faces become the top, left, and back faces. Rotating the entire cube \(180^\circ\) about the vertical axis sends

\[
\text{left}\to\text{right},\qquad \text{back}\to\text{front},\qquad \text{top}\to\text{top}.
\]

After this rotation, the three diagonals coincide exactly with those shown on the top, right, and front faces. This is a genuine rotation, not a reflection.
